review_findings: The Laken Riley House and Senate versions are correctly grouped as one narrow detention-and-enforcement path while preserving the additional Senate-version offenses.
The HALT Fentanyl amendment, initial passage, and later Senate-origin framework are correctly grouped with mixed episode behavior.
The initially overgrouped D.C. youth-sentencing and juvenile-court-transfer actions were correctly split into distinct episodes.
Roll 155 is correctly excluded from primary FISA episode membership because its preserved source-identity conflict materially affects predecessor grouping.
Roll 278 remains unassigned and contributes no unsupported final-passage meaning.
All 35 primary-assigned actions appear exactly once; no action is double-counted.
All five post-freeze benchmark episode comparisons align without a remaining severity finding.
The cumulative launch-risk register properly carries action-level risks and adds the FISA episode-grouping ambiguity.
The 30-item episode calibration population excludes retained ambiguity and no-safe states, and no launch sample has been selected.
All 35 parity-manifest references match final serialized bytes.
